AlternativeChannels: Additional compact channel rows to try as correction sources if the first completion space does not close. Their selected residues must agree with the original targets; they never replace those targets.
BoseSymmetryGroups: Groups of identical external bosons to symmetrize. Automatic infers species and helicity from ordered process metadata and the model; {} disables boson exchange projection without disabling fermion projection.
Build: Whether to configure and compile the exported C++ project against the existing SPINAS library. False writes source files only; a source-only export does not require CMake.
CMakeExecutable: Path to the CMake program used when building. Automatic searches PATH and standard installations, including common macOS application and Homebrew locations.
CalcHEPDirectory: Chosen CalcHEP installation directory. None, the default, leaves the optional backend unconfigured. An explicitly supplied Automatic consults the corresponding environment variables only; no installation path is guessed.
CalcHEPModel: Chosen equivalent CalcHEP reference theory as {directory, modelNumber}. None, the default, selects no theory; Automatic does not infer a model. This reference model is separate from the supplied HEPCAT amplitudes.
CalcHEPPoints: Number of random physical phase-space points compared by the generated independent CalcHEP validation executable. This tests both implementations at the same points.
CalcHEPSeed: Default seed of the generated CalcHEP comparison. Automatic chooses from the time when validation runs and prints the concrete seed; an unsigned 64-bit integer, including zero, makes the run reproducible.
ChannelCompanions: Whether completion first tries a small set of source-derived physical-pole correction directions for eligible two-leg channels. Automatic gives this attempt a bounded share of the existing clock; None skips it. Every original channel must still validate.
ChannelPreparationOptions: Additional PrepareAmplitudes options for the factorization-channel stage of ConstructAmplitude. Original channel expressions remain the residue targets even when their continuations are prepared.
ChannelReferences: Reference-spinor continuations available to factorization completion. Automatic tries a bounded set and verifies each on its selected cut; None restricts the fit to the literal correction space.
CheckOptions: Additional CheckAmplitudes options for the final validation stage of ConstructAmplitude. Disabling a check narrows the validation being claimed.
CorrectionBasis: Explicit correction expressions whose coefficients may be fitted. Automatic uses bounded directions from the supplied diagrams, channels and retained preparation data; it does not invent an unrestricted interaction ansatz.
ExternalParticles: Ordered external particle names when compact amplitude pairs no longer retain the process. Automatic uses recorded metadata or only unambiguous model matches; equal masses alone never establish identical species.
FactorizationOptions: Additional CompleteFactorization options for the factorization-completion stage of ConstructAmplitude. These override stage defaults without changing the original lower-point residue targets.
FermionHelicities: Leg-to-helicity rules or an association specifying massless Dirac external states for Feynman conversion. Required missing massless-fermion helicities are reported rather than guessed.
FermionSymmetryGroups: Groups of identical external fermions to antisymmetrize with permutation parity signs. Automatic uses ordered process metadata and model spin/species declarations; {} disables only fermion exchange projection.
FeynmanAmplitudes: Independent Feynman amplitude expressions or pairs to compare at ordinary off-cut momenta. None omits this extra comparison; it does not disable the constructive physical-pole checks.
FeynmanModel: The independent model used with Feynman amplitudes. In ConstructAmplitude, None omits Feynman generation and an explicit model enables it; in the checker, Automatic uses the appropriate supplied model context when available.
FeynmanPreparationOptions: Additional preparation settings for ConstructAmplitude's independent Feynman benchmark. The complete Feynman diagram sum uses coherent external references and keeps internal lines off shell.
FeynmanSamples: Number of independent phase-space/spin comparisons with the supplied Feynman result. Automatic chooses a bounded count appropriate to the checking workload.
FeynmanTimeConstraint: Time budget for the independent Feynman comparison. Automatic resolves a bounded allowance; a timeout is reported as unresolved, not as agreement.
FinalPreparationOptions: Additional PrepareAmplitudes options for the completed amplitude. This final stage has external mass rules only and never applies internal-line on-shell assumptions.
FixedHelicities: Massless leg-to-doubled-helicity rules selecting states in the grouped SPINAS exporter. Automatic retains the requested coverage; explicitly fixed incoming helicities are not averaged over, and a fixed outgoing helicity is a labeled contribution.
HighEnergyBound: Maximum allowed power of energy with masses fixed. Automatic uses the renormalizable tree target E^(4-n); provide a justified different bound for another theory or normalization.
HighEnergyCheck: Whether to test high-energy scaling of the complete amplitude. Automatic runs the applicable built-in check; False omits it and therefore narrows the reported validation.
HighEnergyOptions: Additional CompleteHighEnergy options used by ConstructAmplitude after physical factorization completion. Only retained or explicitly supplied correction freedom is fitted.
HighEnergySamples: Number of independent kinematic directions/spin assignments sampled for high-energy scaling. More samples improve numerical evidence but do not turn the check into a symbolic proof.
HighEnergyTimeConstraint: Time budget for the high-energy diagnostic. Automatic chooses a bounded allowance; unresolved scaling or a timeout is not counted as a pass.
IncomingLegs: External leg labels that are physically incoming in exported C++. Other legs are crossed once from HEPCAT's all-ingoing convention, including outgoing angle-spinor signs. Runnable projects currently require two incoming particles.
InputReweighting: Whether factorization completion first fits a scale on the pole-bearing input and a small overlap-reduced candidate. Automatic proposes these bounded corrections and validates them; None skips them. It is not a rule for averaging diagrams.
InternalOnShell: Whether preparation may use declared constructive internal-channel masses in each item's numerator. True never puts PropDen denominators on shell and never transfers one diagram's assumptions to another; False leaves internal-shell reductions disabled.
KinematicKind: Scope of a supplied physical cut chart: "Sample" for sampled kinematics or "Symbolic" for a symbolic chart. A sampled match is evidence on the chart, not a general analytic identity.
KinematicMap: Function map[expression, channels, poleVariables] evaluating every spinor, momentum and propagator consistently near selected cuts. The checker can construct supported automatic charts; PhysicalPoleResidue with Automatic alone returns a FORMAL structural coefficient.
MaxCandidates: Bound on candidate identity edits considered during preparation. Automatic selects a finite workload-dependent allowance rather than searching every possible route.
MaxCorrectionTerms: Bound on the size of the fitted correction space. Automatic chooses a finite process-dependent limit; explicit values control effort without weakening residue and independent-validation requirements.
MaxExpandedTerms: Maximum number of expanded tensor terms allowed during Feynman-to-spinor conversion. Exceeding the bound reports failure rather than returning an unsupported partial conversion.
MaxKernels: Maximum local Wolfram worker kernels available to parallel stages. Automatic respects processor availability and license limits; 1 requests serial execution. Worker setup and expression transfer can outweigh small jobs.
MaxReferenceChoices: Maximum reference assignments tried during bounded preparation. Automatic currently allows up to 64 trials, subject to the shared reference and item clocks; this is not exhaustive global minimization.
MaxRefinements: Maximum rounds that feed failed independent validation samples back into the simultaneous factorization equations. Each refinement is followed by fresh held-out validation.
MaxSteps: Maximum improving identity-search steps during preparation. Automatic scales the bounded effort to the workload; 0 retains deterministic contraction, spinor and permitted scalar-shell reductions while skipping the search.
MomentumConservation: Whether identities may use the complete declared external momentum sum. The operation uses the known external-leg list rather than imposing unrelated internal cut conditions.
NumeratorOnShellChannels: Declarations recording internal shell conditions used by a supplied DiagramAmplitudeRecords simplification function. Recording them does not itself apply those conditions or change denominators.
OnShellChannels: Internal cuts legal for an explicit identity edit or scramble. Automatic reads the current diagram pair's internal mass rules; use {} for a combined amplitude with no allowed internal-shell identities.
Output: Choose the amount and shape of returned information. Defaults are a compact check table, prepared input forms, a completed {externalMassRules, expression} pair, or a bare constructed expression; "Details" preserves diagnostics and provenance.
Overwrite: Whether existing generated project files may be replaced. False protects an existing SPINAS output directory from accidental overwriting.
Parallelization: Whether independent items or checks may use local Wolfram workers. Automatic uses suitable parallel work within available resources; False requests serial evaluation, and result order is retained.
ParameterRules: Local numerical parameter overrides keyed by model references or string names. Automatic resolves the model's variables and dependent functions; fitting and checks do not assign global values or replace parameters in the symbolic final amplitude.
PolePreference: Reference and representation preference shared by preparation and completion. Automatic compares or inherits admissible choices; "AllPhysical", "AllSpurious" and "Mixed" bias pole forms, while cyclic/common/independent reference choices and None are also available. Required checks remain unchanged.
Precision: Floating-point type used by exported SPINAS code. Automatic reads the local library build configuration; "Double" and "LongDouble" must match the library being linked.
PreparationOptions: Additional PrepareAmplitudes options for ConstructAmplitude's initial diagram preparation. Retained preparation reports preserve discarded terms for completion.
PreparationRemainders: Whether factorization completion first tries grouped discarded preparation terms. Automatic uses only retained provenance and a bounded share of the clock; None skips this route. The original channel targets remain authoritative.
PrintReport: Whether ConstructAmplitude prints the resolved run seed, total timing and final check table before returning its amplitude. False suppresses that final printed report.
ProcessName: Valid C++ identifier for the exported SPINAS class and executable. Choose a readable process name that does not collide with reserved generated members.
ProgressFunction: Optional callback receiving stage progress information. Automatic uses the normal progress display; callbacks are evaluated on the main kernel rather than independently by workers.
ProgressReporting: Whether preparation and construction stages display their progress. False suppresses the live stage display without changing the algebra or validation.
RandomSeed: Random-sampling seed. Automatic resolves one time-based seed for the operation; an explicit integer, including zero, reproduces the sample choices. Detailed reports retain the resolved seed. ComplicateAmplitude uses the legacy symbol key RandomSeed; modern construction/checking functions use the string key "RandomSeed".
RecordSteps: Whether ComplicateAmplitude retains intermediate states and the legal identity edits along its scramble path, rather than returning only the ordinary scrambled result.
ReduceSpinorProducts: Whether Feynman-to-spinor conversion applies ordinary ReduceSpinorProducts identities after converting the tensor structure. These identities do not impose internal-line on-shell conditions.
ReferenceCheck: Whether the checker varies explicit Xi reference spinors. Automatic runs the applicable test; if no Xi remains, the report records no explicit dependence rather than claiming an additional analytic Ward-identity proof.
ReferenceSamples: Number of reference-spinor comparisons on conserved external kinematics. These comparisons hold the physical phase-space point fixed while changing admissible references.
ReferenceSpinors: Explicit leg-to-reference rules or an association for Feynman-to-spinor conversion. Automatic introduces independent Xi references; use another eligible massless leg or an explicit Spinor. This lower-level conversion option is separate from the workflow's PolePreference.
ReferenceTimeConstraint: Budget for reference comparisons in checking, or reference-choice search in preparation. Automatic bounds this work; preparation shares it with the remaining per-item clock rather than adding an unlimited extra search.
RepresentativeSelection: Whether completion chooses a simpler particular point inside an already validated affine family. Automatic performs bounded exact coefficient cancellations while preserving its directions and explicit regular input; None retains the original particular point.
ReturnDetails: Whether to expose optional diagnostic data instead of the compact default result. For preparation and factorization completion it retains provenance, directions and validation and takes precedence over Output; for export it returns file paths and build/run results.
RunCalcHEPValidation: Whether export builds and runs the generated independent CalcHEP comparison. It uses the same physical points on both implementations; unsupported polarized or color-stripped comparisons report unavailable. When MadGraph is also requested, its check still runs if CalcHEP fails. A failed requested reference returns Failure with both reports retained in ExportResult.
RunExamples: Whether to build the exported SPINAS project and execute its sample phase-space points. True implies the necessary build step.
SPINASDirectory: Path to the local SPINAS checkout/library. Automatic searches SPINAS_ROOT and the sibling spinas checkout; an explicit directory selects another installation.
Samples: Number of physical cut samples or fitting samples, depending on the stage. Automatic completion settings choose a bounded process-dependent count; successful fitting is followed by separate validation samples.
ShiftedChannelContinuations: Whether completion tries bounded two-null-leg continuation proposals as correction directions. Automatic restricts the attempt to its supported eligibility; False or None disables it. Each direction is checked on its own cut and no vanishing large-shift boundary is assumed.
ShowPropagatorExpressions: Whether drawn diagrams display their propagator expressions. False keeps the diagram picture compact.
ShowVertexExpressions: Whether drawn diagrams display the assigned vertex expressions. False shows the simpler topology and particle labels.
SimplificationFunction: Transformation applied to each DiagramAmplitudeRecords pair {massRules, expression}. Identity leaves it unchanged; a custom function must preserve exactly the same mass rules, with propagators protected.
SpuriousPoles: Apparent nonphysical poles to test. Automatic discovers denominator factors not accounted for by the supplied physical channels; {} disables these tests instead of certifying cancellation.
StructuralCoefficient: Whether PhysicalPoleResidue also computes its opaque-propagator coefficient. True includes that optional formal result; False saves the work and stores Missing["NotRequested"] without skipping physical chart validation.
TimeConstraint: Maximum elapsed time allowed by the operation or stage. Where Automatic is supported it selects a finite workload-dependent budget; explicit seconds or supported Infinity override it. A timeout is reported, never treated as a successful amplitude.
Tolerance: Numerical comparison tolerance for sampled amplitudes and residues. Exact cancellations remain exact; tightening a tolerance does not remove floating-point conditioning problems near singular points.
UncutChannels: Other known physical channels that must remain generic while the selected cut is imposed. The chart validator rejects unintended extra cuts or incompatible external data.
ValidationParameterRules: Additional or automatically selected local parameter assignments used in independent completion validation. They help detect fits tied accidentally to one numerical mass or coupling point without changing the symbolic result.
ValidationSamples: Number of held-out samples used after fitting correction coefficients. Automatic chooses a bounded workload-dependent allowance; these samples are distinct from the fitting equations.
ChannelMass: Mass of the selected internal channel in the older x-factor reducers. This is a legacy symbol option and supplies a declared numerator identity, not an instruction to set propagator denominators on shell.
ChannelMomenta: External labels defining the selected channel in the older x-factor reducers. This legacy symbol option works with ChannelMass and Momenta.
InternalLineOnShell: Whether the older SimplifySpinorProducts helper may additionally use the stated InternalLines shell. False is the default; ordinary ReduceSpinorProducts does not acquire an internal-shell assumption.
InternalLines: External labels composing the internal line used by the older SimplifySpinorProducts helper. It matters only when the corresponding internal-shell reductions are enabled and its mass rules are supplied.
InternalMasses: Mass replacement rules supplied to the older compact-string amplitude converters. This is a legacy symbol option, distinct from model-local numerical ParameterRules.
Momenta: Complete external momentum labels available to the older simplification or x-factor helper. This is a legacy symbol option; the list supplies the context needed for momentum-conservation identities.
PrintWarnings: Whether the older SimplifySpinorProducts helper prints warnings about its iterative simplification. This legacy symbol option affects messages rather than the allowed physical assumptions.
massReplacementRules: Explicit Mass[...] replacement rules for the older SimplifySpinorProducts helper. Supply only assumptions justified for the current item; do not combine incompatible diagram-local shells.
nTimes: Maximum number of repeated simplification rounds in the older SimplifySpinorProducts helper. This is a legacy symbol option, not a wall-clock limit.
MadGraphDirectory: Chosen MadGraph installation directory. None, the default, leaves reference validation disabled. An explicitly supplied Automatic consults environment variables only; pass a path to make the selection explicit.
MadGraphModel: Chosen equivalent MadGraph UFO model name or directory. None, the default, selects no reference theory. Automatic does not infer a theory. Specify the model and any particle filter explicitly.
MadGraphParameterRules: Real numerical values for named external MadGraph UFO parameters. Automatic uses the supported model-parameter matching; explicit rules supply otherwise ambiguous independent inputs.
RunMadGraphValidation: Whether WriteSPINASProcess builds and runs the independent MadGraph comparison. False writes the optional support without running it; True runs a report for each exported massless-helicity combination. A numerical FAIL is returned as Failure, not a successful source-export result. If CalcHEP is also requested, both checks are attempted and their reports remain in ExportResult.
MadGraphPoints: Number of common random phase-space points compared for each massless-helicity combination. The default is 1000.
MadGraphSeed: Random seed for the generated MadGraph comparison. Automatic chooses one time-based seed when validation runs and reports it; an explicit unsigned 64-bit integer, including zero, replays the samples.
RelativeTolerance: Maximum relative numerical difference allowed by the selected comparison. ValidateMadGraph defaults to 10^-7; this is applied independently to each tested massless-helicity combination.
AbsoluteTolerance: Optional absolute numerical comparison tolerance. ValidateMadGraph defaults to zero so a wrong tiny amplitude cannot pass through a fixed absolute floor.
MinimumEnergy: Lower center-of-mass energy used by ValidateMadGraph's random validation samples. Automatic chooses a value above the incoming and outgoing mass thresholds.
MaximumEnergy: Upper center-of-mass energy used by ValidateMadGraph's random validation samples. Automatic chooses a suitable range above threshold.
MadGraphParameterMap: Rules mapping HEPCAT model parameter names to external or derived MadGraph UFO parameter names. Automatic uses supported same-name and known-model matching; unresolved used parameters prevent a passing comparison.

ValidateMadGraph.TimeConstraint: Time budget in seconds for generating and compiling the independent MadGraph reference process. A timeout is an incomplete check, not PASS.

MadGraphAllowedParticles: All retains the full selected MadGraph theory. A nonempty list of unique positive absolute PDG codes, such as {11,22}, restricts the reference particle sector and includes antiparticles. Every external particle type must be present.
CalcHEPAllowedParticles: All retains the full selected CalcHEP theory. A nonempty list of unique positive absolute PDG codes restricts the independent reference particle sector, including antiparticles. Every external type must be included.
